industry.why: Underweight, from Double Underweight, on the row's own written condition ('to D on a European consumer reading that is not falling, or the industry back at C with Online retail holding A'): the tape leg is met, industry relative strength C (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; F prior) with Online retail A for a third reading. The reasoned read agrees in direction: US consumer confidence jumped 11.4 points to 103.3 (Goldman Sachs, 25-Nov), Goldman's Jaisson (20-Nov) favours Retailers and Bell (20-Nov) wants 'Domestic not Defensive' in the UK, and the 27-Nov-26 regime (risk-off in the open, led by the AI capital-spending unwind and its credit leg) has the consumer away from the epicentre the Double Underweight was set for. Not Neutral because Stehn (Goldman, 22-Nov) expects high energy prices to slow euro area consumption over winter, France is contracting (PMI 46.2) and no European consumer survey was read. The sector rows beneath hold their letters. One live holding (D'Ieteren 2.66%); 20 Pool stocks. Counter-case: lifting a consumer row on the tape in an open risk-off with the European consumer unread is early. Back to F on a European consumer reading that is falling; to C on one that is not falling with Online retail holding A.

sector.key: H.4. Retail - online and delivery platforms
sector.why: Underweight, carried, with the sharpest disagreement in the consumer industry: relative strength A for a third reading (27-Nov-26 against 25-Sep-26, not week on week; A prior), which this week fired the industry's lift to D; the row's own condition (a European consumer reading that is not falling) was not read. Pool names Allegro, Delivery Hero. Counter-case: three readings at A is a trend, and Jaisson favours Retailers. To C on a European consumer reading that is not falling.

geography.why: Overweight, from Neutral, on the first country-specific evidence since the row was set: Germany's composite PMI is 55.0, a 56-month high (Goldman Economics, 24-Nov; S&P Global via Pivotus, 23-Nov), with automation data points turning up (Rockwell, Siemens Digital Industries; Danske, 26-Nov) and Bunds forecast at 3.1% by end-2027 (Marshall, 22-Nov); the signed Lists statement asks for a country view wherever there is evidence, and this week there is. Eleven Pool stocks are German-listed. Counter-case: one PMI print is one month, the US tariff lands on the EU at 15% inclusive, Stehn's winter energy squeeze applies to the euro area, and the German Pool names (Bayer, Symrise, Evonik, Talanx, Sartorius, Deutsche Borse among them) are global businesses on which a country letter is a blunt instrument. Back to C on a German PMI read under 52 or a second month of euro area services PMIs falling.
